detailed_description:

The target video uses realistic live-action commercial cinematography with a premium advertising aesthetic. The scene should look like authentic professional camera footage rather than an AI-generated image, illustration, animation, or CGI render.

The environment is a refined high-end commercial presentation space with clean visual design, professional three-point lighting, realistic materials, controlled reflections, subtle depth of field, and cinematic spatial separation. The background remains visually stable and unobtrusive so that the presenter and product remain the primary focus.

[Shot 1] The video begins with <Subject 1> standing naturally in the commercial environment, facing directly toward the camera. Her face is clearly visible and remains consistent with <Picture 1>. Her body, hairstyle, clothing, posture, and product-holding position follow <Picture 2>.

The framing is a stable medium shot. The composition clearly includes the presenter's face, upper body, both hands, and the complete product. The product must remain sufficiently large and clear in the frame for the viewer to recognize its shape, materials, packaging, and important visual details.

<Subject 1> establishes direct eye contact with the center of the camera lens. Her gaze should feel focused, confident, warm, and conversational rather than empty or expressionless. She behaves as though she is speaking directly to a real customer standing in front of her.

Audio 1 is the exclusive source of the spoken performance. <Subject 1> (S1) delivers the complete spoken content contained in Audio 1 directly to the camera. Do not invent, replace, shorten, paraphrase, add, or remove any spoken content from Audio 1.

The timing, rhythm, pronunciation, pauses, breathing intervals, speaking speed, emphasis, emotional cadence, and total duration of the spoken performance must follow Audio 1 precisely.

The presenter's mouth must remain naturally synchronized with Audio 1 throughout the entire speech. Lip movement, mouth opening, lip shape, jaw movement, and facial articulation must correspond naturally to the actual Chinese speech. Do not produce delayed lip movement, frozen lips, unrelated mouth movement, exaggerated mouth opening, or speech that appears disconnected from the audio.

During short pauses and breathing transitions in Audio 1, her lips may remain naturally slightly parted or transition subtly between phonemes instead of abruptly snapping completely closed. When speech resumes, articulation continues naturally from the previous mouth position.

While speaking, <Subject 1> performs continuous realistic physiological micro-movements. Her shoulders rise and fall subtly with natural breathing. Her torso makes extremely small and believable posture adjustments. Her weight shifts very slightly between her feet rather than remaining perfectly fixed in one position.

Her head occasionally performs a small natural nod to emphasize important spoken phrases. The nods are restrained and irregular rather than repetitive. She naturally blinks approximately once every 3–5 seconds while maintaining engagement with the camera. Her facial expression subtly follows the emotional tone and delivery of Audio 1.

The presenter must never appear completely frozen or mechanically animated. At the same time, the movement must never become exaggerated, theatrical, repetitive, or overly energetic. The overall performance should resemble a real professional presenter naturally speaking to a customer.

<Subject 1> holds <Subject 2> naturally with both hands in front of her upper torso. One hand primarily supports the lower portion of the product while the other hand naturally assists the presentation.

Her fingers remain anatomically correct with realistic joints, curvature, gripping pressure, and contact with the product. The fingers should never become unnaturally straight, rigid, fused, duplicated, elongated, or disconnected. The hands must physically conform to the actual shape of <Subject 2>.

The presenter does not keep both hands completely motionless. While continuing to support the product, she performs small natural wrist rotations and subtle changes in hand orientation. These movements gently reveal different surfaces or features of the product.

The assisting hand may briefly make a small presentation gesture, such as lightly indicating the product edge, gently touching a visible feature, slightly opening the palm beside the product, or adjusting its grip. The gesture amplitude remains small, refined, controlled, and ergonomically plausible.

The hand movements should naturally follow the rhythm and emphasis of Audio 1 without mechanically matching every syllable. Important spoken phrases may be accompanied by a subtle wrist adjustment, slight product rotation, small hand gesture, or restrained head nod.

When the presenter changes the product orientation, the movement must originate naturally from her wrists, elbows, shoulders, and fingers. The product should move together with her hands rather than rotating independently.

<Subject 2> remains physically stable during all hand movements. Its structure, geometry, dimensions, packaging, colors, surface details, printed graphics, labels, logos, and visible text remain unchanged.

The product may make tiny natural positional adjustments caused by the presenter's grip and wrist movement, but it must never independently deform or move. It must not bend, stretch, melt, duplicate, disappear, or morph into another object.

The product's highlights and reflections change naturally according to the small changes in its orientation relative to the lighting. Reflections should appear physically plausible and continuous rather than flashing, flickering, or changing randomly.

During the main portion of the presentation, the presenter may gently rotate <Subject 2> a small amount toward the camera to emphasize its appearance. The movement is slow and deliberate, allowing the viewer to clearly see the product. Her fingers naturally adjust their grip during the rotation.

After the brief presentation gesture, she smoothly returns <Subject 2> to a comfortable centered position in front of her torso. The product remains fully visible and unobstructed.

The camera performs an extremely slow cinematic Dolly In throughout the shot. The camera movement should resemble the subtle breathing rhythm of a real professional camera operator rather than a perfectly mechanical linear translation.

The camera movement remains extremely small and smooth. There is no sudden zoom, orbit, shake, rotation, or change of perspective. The framing gradually becomes slightly closer while still maintaining a medium composition that includes the presenter's face, upper body, both hands, and the complete product.

The background remains optically stable. Only a very subtle change in depth of field occurs as the camera slowly approaches, creating a natural sense of spatial depth without distracting from the presenter or product.

Professional three-point lighting remains consistent throughout the entire shot. A soft key light naturally illuminates the presenter's face, a controlled fill light preserves facial detail and natural skin tone, and a subtle rim or separation light separates her from the background.

The presenter's skin must retain realistic pores, fine skin texture, natural tonal variation, and subtle facial detail. Avoid excessive smoothing, artificial beauty filters, waxy skin, plastic skin, overly bright skin, unnatural facial symmetry, or CGI-like facial rendering.

The eyes should contain realistic catchlights and subtle natural movement. The presenter should maintain believable eye contact with the camera without staring unnaturally or keeping the eyes completely motionless.

The woman's face must remain the same person as <Picture 1> throughout the entire video. Do not generate a different woman who merely resembles <Picture 1>. Do not alter her face shape, eye shape, eye spacing, eyebrows, nose, lips, chin, facial proportions, skin tone, or apparent age.

Do not perform face slimming, eye enlargement, nose reshaping, lip enlargement, artificial beautification, excessive symmetry, facial smoothing, identity replacement, or facial redesign.

<Picture 2> must not override the facial identity from <Picture 1>. The facial appearance of the woman in <Picture 2> is only a secondary visual reference for the complete body presentation and must not become the identity source.

The product must remain the same product as <Picture 2> throughout the video. Do not change its geometry, dimensions, packaging, colors, material, printed graphics, logos, labels, or visible text.

Printed text and product markings should remain stable and legible whenever they are visible. Do not rewrite, distort, scramble, duplicate, or randomly replace text.

Hand anatomy remains consistent throughout the entire shot. No extra fingers, missing fingers, fused fingers, elongated fingers, broken wrists, unnatural joint rotations, duplicated hands, floating hands, or fingers passing through the product.

The presenter's body, face, clothing, hairstyle, hands, product, lighting, environment, and composition remain visually consistent from beginning to end.

The entire video is one continuous shot with no cuts, no abrupt transitions, no sudden camera changes, and no character or product identity drift.

The overall performance should feel natural, confident, persuasive, premium, and human. The presenter should appear to genuinely understand and demonstrate the product while communicating directly with the viewer, rather than simply standing still and reading an advertisement.

overall_soundscape:

A clean premium commercial recording environment with subtle room ambience. Audio 1 remains the dominant and authoritative speech source throughout the entire video. The presenter's natural breathing and very faint clothing movement may be audible beneath the speech when appropriate. Subtle fabric sounds and delicate hand-to-product contact sounds may occur naturally during product handling but must never interfere with Audio 1.

There should be no competing dialogue, no additional speaker, no invented voice, and no background sound that interferes with speech clarity.

non_diegetic_music:

A restrained premium commercial music bed with subtle cinematic electronic-acoustic textures at a slow to moderate tempo. The music remains very low in volume throughout the presentation and never competes with Audio 1. It supports the polished commercial atmosphere while keeping the presenter's speech completely clear and intelligible. The music may subtly rise during visual product presentation moments but should remain subordinate to the voice.
